title: Latent Feature Spark Log
content:
Purpose: informal capture of 12 small feature seeds (latents) that might increase product stickiness or cut token spend in narrow flows. Not formal PRD — more a gardener's log. Use this to decide 2–3 pilots for Q1 experiments.

Format: each entry = name, 1-line hypothesis, rough user story, quick acceptance metric, sketch of experiment, blockers. Keep terse.

1) Session Peek Presets
- Hypothesis: Exposing 2–3 prebuilt session fidelity presets (concise / normal / vivid) will reduce average tokens per session by ~8% while keeping NPS stable for task-based apps.
- User story: As a product dev, I want a simple flag per session so I can offer a low-cost "concise" mode to price-sensitive customers.
- Acceptance: average tokens/session drops 6–10% in sample cohort, user task success >= 95% of control.
- Experiment: A/B on 5k sessions over 2 weeks, instrument per-token cost and surface an opt-in toggle in the demo dashboard.
- Blockers: need UX for toggle, rolloutable on Hosted API only.

2) Microprompt Snippets Library (Local)
- Hypothesis: A lightweight, client-side snippet library reduces repeated prompt verbosity and reduces send-token size by ~4–6% for pro users.
- User story: As an engineer, I want a snippet API to assemble common instruction blocks client-side before submission.
- Acceptance: snippet usage rate > 25% in cohort and token reduction observed.
- Experiment: ship JS helper + small opt-in sample, track usage via telemetry.
- Blockers: telemetry privacy concerns; need opt-in flag.

3) Prefetch Warmup Hinting
- Hypothesis: A tiny 1–2 token hint sent asynchronously prior to heavy-turns reduces first-token latency by 8–12% for cold sessions without large cost.
- User story: As an SRE, I want predictable p95 for first token in chat flows.
- Acceptance: p95 first-token improves by target, cost delta < 0.5%.
- Experiment: background prefetch for 10% traffic; measure p50/p95 and cost.
- Blockers: routing complexity; interaction with KV cache.

4) Response Quanta Profiles (beta)
- Hypothesis: Letting devs choose response quanta (tiny/normal/expanded) will let teams tradeoff succinctness vs completeness with measurable cost/QoQ effects.
- User story: As a dev, I want to set a default quanta per route to control downstream UI flicker and token spend.
- Acceptance: teams can hit 10–20% cost variance with predictable quality.
- Experiment: add parameter to hosted API + SDK; collect quality regressions via eval set.
- Blockers: eval harness integration.

5) Tiny Fallback Model Snippet
- Hypothesis: Short, templated fallback summaries (1–2 sentences) from a cheap model reduce user escapes and perceived errors.
- User story: As a product manager, I want graceful degradations that still feel helpful.
- Acceptance: reduction in session abandonment by >4%.
- Experiment: route overflow to quantized model with a canned template.
- Blockers: voice/brand consistency; SLA changes.

6) Prompt Provenance Tagging (developer UX)
- Hypothesis: Adding a short provenance header (which snippet / template / user) helps debugging and reduces iteration time for prompt tuning.
- User story: As an engineer, I want to see which authoring template produced the prompt in logs.
- Acceptance: time-to-debug per issue drops 20%.
- Experiment: add header metadata to dev console traces, anonymize for customers.
- Blockers: privacy / redaction policy work.

7) Session Glue Tokens (economy lane)
- Hypothesis: Insert compact session summary tokens maintained server-side to reconstruct context will enable aggressive client-side trimming without losing coherence for a majority of sessions.
- User story: As a product dev on budget plan, I want to reduce tokens sent while preserving continuity for <8-turn interactions.
- Acceptance: 30–40% reduction in average tokens for trimmed flows, no drop in task success for short dialogues.
- Experiment: synthetic replay on recorded conversations to test reconstruction fidelity, then small live test.
- Blockers: serialization format; migration path for private deployments.

8) Inline Eval Hooks
- Hypothesis: Lightweight per-request eval labels (accept/clarify) from client will let us detect regressions earlier.
- User story: As an applied ML engineer, I want cheap signal from users in the UI to feed quality dashboards.
- Acceptance: meaningful signal in >5% of requests for targeted flows.
- Experiment: small SDK change with 1-click feedback UI; instrument retention.
- Blockers: noise filtering and incentive design.

9) Microbatch Hinting API
- Hypothesis: Allowing clients to hint grouping boundaries improves batching efficiency on Dedicated and reduces cost slightly without harming latency for many workloads.
- User story: As infra, I want clients to opt-in to microbatch boundary hints when they can tolerate small added latency.
- Acceptance: batch utilization up by X% and unit cost reduces 3–5% for participating tenants.
- Experiment: define hint param in SDK; test on Trusted Dedicated pools.
- Blockers: misuse and fairness across tenants.

10) Compact Rewrites Service (edge)
- Hypothesis: A small preprocessor that rewrites verbose user messages into compact canonical form reduces tokens while preserving intent.
- User story: As an edge developer, I want a hook that compresses user inputs before sending to the model.
- Acceptance: upstream token counts drop 12–18% and intent-preservation metric > 95%.
- Experiment: local rewrite model as a thin service; AB test on chat app.
- Blockers: hallucination risk in rewrite; privacy/anonymization.

11) Cost-limited REPL for Prompting
- Hypothesis: A dev-facing REPL that simulates token cost and response quanta will shorten prompt tuning iteration and surface cost tradeoffs.
- User story: As an engineer, I want to prototype prompts with live cost estimates.
- Acceptance: time-to-deploy decreases; adoption by >40% of internal teams.
- Experiment: internal beta tool, track adoption.
- Blockers: surface area for instrumentation.

12) Micro UX: "Why this answer?" toggle
- Hypothesis: A small, user-visible explanation toggle that runs a constrained trace improves trust and reduces repeat follow-ups.
- User story: As an end user, I want an optional short explanation so I can understand model thinking when needed.
- Acceptance: reduction in clarification follow-ups by >6% for enabled users.
- Experiment: client-side toggle that triggers a limited extra call for explanation.
- Blockers: cost overhead; crafting short, non-misleading explanations.

Cross-cutting priorities and notes:
- Privacy & redaction: any feature adding provenance or headers must have opt-out and redaction paths for PII. Add a separate TODO to align with privacy team. (See linked_artifacts JIRA-PRIV-19)
- Eval harness: majority of these need a micro-eval set. Start by assembling 200 canonical prompts for 3 target flows: knowledge Q&A, transactional chat, summarization.
- Rollout surface: prefer Hosted API for initial pilots; Dedicated-only features need sales sync. Private deployment requirements should be listed before any non-backwards compatible server-side format changes.
- Quick wins: Session Peek Presets, Prompt Provenance Tagging, and Cost-limited REPL look feasible in 6–8 weeks with small eng effort.

Immediate next steps (my TODOs):
- Sketch API params for Session Peek Presets + SDK examples (Clara) — due 2026-02-27
- Chat with Mika about eval harness and set up shared seed prompts (Ravi + Clara) — scheduled 2026-02-24
- Privacy sync with legal to validate provenance headers (Evelyn) — request meeting
- Create JIRA epics: LATENT-100, LATENT-101, LATENT-102 (put behind "experiment" flag)

Open questions / risks to surface:
- Which of these features will conflict with existing cache/keying design? (platform-eng TODO)
- Are there billing implications (metering line items) for tiny background hints or extra explanation calls?
- How do presets interact with function-calling and streaming? Edge cases to test.

Notes to self: keep these short experiments isolated behind flags so we can measure unit economics easily. Revisit monthly and prune the list to top 3 winners.

End of log.
